Second cousins with the full derivation through Emmet/Orra and Roy/Duncan

Gideon Vose, his father, not nephew

Gives 16.27/17.6 = 0.9244 and 7.56 percent short; key requires 0.95 / 95 percent / one part in twenty

67,000 lb instead of 76,000 lb
$19,600 and 19.4 percent instead of $19,000 and 20 percent; both required exactly

$95.00 from 380 lb at 25 cents; key requires $86.40 (360 x $0.24)

$77.93 with the line items; $77.39 mentioned only as the Chronicle's discrepancy and rejected in E
72 pipettes correct but shortfall per pipette given as 1.33 c.c.; both required

Variable named: the glass pipette, own measure replaced by a borrowed one
Constants: herds, pasture/season, machinery, same tester, same supervision
Nine weeks, 8 May to 10 July, tests markedly higher and falling back the day his own glass returned; no 3.80/3.61 figures but the nine weeks and the result are right
Both halves: locates the cause in the glass rather than herds/feed/tester's honesty, and states limits (no size of error, no identification of the defect)
Three distinct reasons — 1911 interval (r22), station-gain ledger (r23), Strawn's lactometer visits (r22/r18) — attributed to named narrators
Explicitly argues independence (experimental / documentary / external oversight) and states all three would hold without the 1958 measurement
A09: headline verdict 'Did the bookkeeper question the ledger entries? No.' — an assertion, not an abstention
Answers the literal question yes, citing the 1902 complaints and the 1919 circular

REQUIRED three of five: only the signed ledger sheets carrying the station gain and the 1919 circular qualify; manager-from-1913 is given wrongly as 1911, watering-at-the-hearing and the never-names-glassware point are absent
A03: no declared inability on whether he knew the tests were understated. No -2: the sheet's claims stay on the item-1 side (he knew the tests ran low, did not investigate the cause)

Capped. Three-plus conflicts found, correctly resolved with a stated method: invoice $77.39 vs $77.93 (document), Kyle's June 1922 vs 12 June 1923 (corroboration + the 1924 rise), $3,500 vs $3,800 (record over 52-year-old memory); also great-niece/granddaughter and first-cousin-once-removed/second-cousins beyond the cap
No near-tie pair identified anywhere: every wrong value is attributed to a single narrator, so the two-carriers condition is never met

A04 earned: 'What happened to the specific lot ... remains unclear from the sources', with Ammon's regrind flagged as speculation and the burned 1931 works records noted. A06 (whose measure was borrowed) and A10 (when butterfat payment began) never raised
Explicitly catches Kyle refuting himself on his own arithmetic: '[error on his part: 40M / 25 years = 1.6M, not 1.4M]'
Right cause, wrong size: 16.27 c.c. and 7.56 percent rather than 16.72 and 95 percent of true; never derives 0.19 as 5 percent of 3.80, and its cessation evidence is the corrupted 3.85
Watering named to Vose and defeated by Strawn's lactometer visits and the 1911 interval
Theft named and defeated specifically by the 1911 borrowed-measure interval with the same man at the bench
Bog hay named (1908 committee, the 1926 veterinarian) and defeated by Bulletin 214's five hundredths in winter and nothing in summer against a flat 0.19
A07: headline verdict 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.' — an assertion
A05: headline verdict 'Ansel Keddie suspected the glass' — an assertion resting on one uncorroborated recollection
149 words, within the 150-word cap

Decoys correctly rejected, but the summary prints 16.27 c.c. as a headline figure
